ai.description: *Micrixalus sairandhri* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored belly. It is distinguished by a prominent white throat patch and a habit of foot-flagging in fast-flowing streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus sairandhri* is best distinguished by its unique, vibrant reddish-brown dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct dark markings found on other dancing frogs.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus sairandhri* inhabits the wet evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky, shaded streams at altitudes above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, male *Micrixalus sairandhri* perform a unique "foot-flagging" display, extending and waving their hind legs to attract mates and signal rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus sairandhri* is an egg-laying species that breeds during the monsoon season, depositing small clutches of eggs in stream-bed crevices.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus sairandhri* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation streams within the Silent Valley National Park.
ai.callDescription: The Sairandhri Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rapid series of short, metallic chirps, typically heard near fast-flowing, rocky streams in the Western Ghats.
